name: deduction
quote: It must have been a bird because of the feather on the ground.
description: Ability to identify an unknown attribute of an object from general knowledge.

variations.name: inductive reasoning
variations.description: The application of previously learned patterns to a new situation. We can get 'induction' and 'deduction' confused because we can 'deduce' a general pattern from repeated observations.
perceptions: Need to figure out a new situation.
Several parts of the situation partly match past scenarios.
results: Apply similarities from past generalizations as initial guesses about the new situation.

variations.name: logical deduction
variations.description: Identifying an unknown attribute by applying only general principles that have been verified as true, either by definition or comprehensive proof. Few things in complex environments like the social world have bulletproof general principles.
perceptions: Need to figure out a new situation.
There's a set of proven patterns and a process for combining them.
results: Apply proven principles to the new situation.
examples: You know the movie starts at noon, but previews take 10 minutes, so you won't be late if you're there at 12:10.

commentaries.quote: Using mental shortcuts is the only way our simple brains can navigate a world that's more complicated then they are. It may be helpful to have a sense of humility about the quality of the patterns and beliefs you rely on.

4,3,2,1.description: The brain makes a prediction based on combining multiple patterns that were created from one or more experiences.

4.description: A process of applying a disciplined set of known truths in a particular way to arrive at a statement that is likely to be true.
